name: Transformer architecture
bottleneck: Before Transformer architecture, training sequence models on long contexts was impossible or impractical because recurrent networks processed tokens sequentially and could not be parallelized.

Q1.evidence: The Transformer reached state-of-the-art translation quality while training for only 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a regime recurrent models could not match at that quality.
Q1.falsification: this pass dies if recurrent models of 2017 are shown to have matched Transformer quality and training cost at scale

Q2.evidence: Transformers became the substrate for BERT, GPT, ViT and multimodal models, unblocking a whole family of previously impractical systems.
Q2.source: Attention Is All You Need
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if post-2017 large models are shown to rest mainly on non-Transformer architectures

Q3.evidence: Every major LLM core behind 2023 agents, including GPT-4 class systems, is a Transformer variant.
Q3.falsification: this pass dies if a 2023-class agent is shown to have emerged on a non-Transformer core at comparable capability

name: Stored-program architecture
bottleneck: Before the stored-program architecture, general-purpose computation was impractical because machines had to be physically rewired or reconfigured for each new task.

Q1.evidence: The von Neumann design made a single machine able to run any program held in memory, making universal reprogrammable computation possible at all.
Q1.source: First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC
Q1.falsification: This pass dies if general-purpose computing was already practical on fixed-function or plugboard machines.

Q2.evidence: Stored-program computers unblocked every subsequent form of software, from operating systems to neural network training to agent loops.
Q2.source: First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if later computing paradigms did not run as stored programs.

Q3.evidence: Every model, tool and agent loop in the actual history runs on stored-program machines; no alternative substrate produced general computing.
Q3.source: First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC
Q3.falsification: This pass dies if a non-stored-program architecture carried mainstream computing instead.

name: Cross-entropy loss
bottleneck: Before cross-entropy loss, scoring a predicted distribution against reality was impossible or impractical because there was no principled loss measuring distributional mismatch for training classifiers.

Q2.evidence: Cross-entropy is the training objective for classifiers, language models and many structured prediction systems across machine learning.
Q2.source: Entropy (information theory) (Wikipedia)
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if major classifier and language model families are shown to train on unrelated objectives

Q3.evidence: Next-token pre-training of every GPT-class model is defined as minimizing cross-entropy loss.
Q3.falsification: this pass dies if GPT-class pre-training is shown to use a different primary objective

name: Word2vec embeddings
bottleneck: Before word2vec embeddings, representing word meaning for computation was impossible or impractical at scale because sparse count-based vectors were high-dimensional and training neural word vectors was slow.

Q2.evidence: Word2vec vectors improved performance across analogy, similarity and downstream NLP tasks and were adopted throughout industry within a few years.
Q2.source: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if word2vec vectors are shown not to have transferred beyond the analogy task

name: CUDA
bottleneck: Before CUDA, using GPU parallelism for general computation was impossible or impractical because graphics hardware could only be programmed through graphics APIs not designed for it.

Q1.evidence: CUDA gave general-purpose code direct access to GPU parallel cores, making GPU matrix computation practical for non-graphics programmers.
Q1.falsification: this pass dies if general-purpose GPU computing is shown to have been equally accessible through graphics APIs before 2007

Q2.evidence: CUDA enabled GPU acceleration across deep learning, molecular dynamics, finance and scientific simulation.
Q2.source: CUDA (Wikipedia)
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if CUDA use is shown to be confined to deep learning

Q3.evidence: Frontier LLM training runs execute overwhelmingly on NVIDIA GPUs programmed through the CUDA ecosystem.
Q3.falsification: this pass dies if frontier LLM training is shown to run mainly on non-CUDA hardware at comparable scale

name: Gradient descent
bottleneck: Before gradient descent, minimizing a complex function was impractical because there was no general iterative rule that used local slope information to improve a solution step by step.

Q1.evidence: Gradient descent made training parameterized models possible at all by giving a general procedure for minimizing a differentiable loss, the procedure every neural network is trained with.
Q1.falsification: This pass dies if neural networks were historically trained by a non-iterative closed-form method.

Q2.evidence: Gradient-based optimization unblocked all of deep learning, training models from perceptrons to large language models.
Q2.source: Gradient descent - Wikipedia
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if deep learning's models are not trained by gradient methods.

name: Linnainmaa's automatic differentiation
bottleneck: Before Linnainmaa's automatic differentiation, exact gradients of nested functions were impractical because numerical differentiation was inaccurate and symbolic differentiation blew up in expression size.

Q1.evidence: Linnainmaa's 1970 thesis gave reverse-mode differentiation, computing exact derivatives of a nested function in a single backward pass proportional to function evaluation cost.
Q1.source: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors
Q1.falsification: This pass dies if an equally efficient exact gradient method for nested functions predates 1970.

Q2.evidence: Reverse-mode autodiff underlies training of every modern neural network, from MLPs to billion-parameter transformers.
Q2.source: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if large networks were in practice trained by a method independent of reverse-mode gradients.

Q3.evidence: For models with millions of parameters and one scalar loss, reverse mode is asymptotically the only tractable exact gradient method; finite differences would need one evaluation per parameter.
Q3.source: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors
Q3.falsification: This pass dies if a comparably cheap alternative gradient method exists for scalar-loss, many-parameter models.

name: Attention mechanism (Bahdanau)
bottleneck: Before the attention mechanism, neural sequence models were impractical on long inputs because a single fixed-length vector had to carry the entire source sequence.

Q1.evidence: Bahdanau attention let the decoder align to relevant source words at each step, restoring translation quality on long sentences that fixed-vector seq2seq models lost.
Q1.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - arXiv
Q1.falsification: This pass dies if fixed-vector models matched attention models on long sentences in the original comparisons.

Q2.evidence: Generalizing attention to self-attention produced the Transformer, which unblocked modern LLMs and hence LLM agents.
Q2.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - arXiv
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if the Transformer's self-attention is shown to derive independently of Bahdanau-style alignment.

Q3.evidence: Every production LLM agent runs on a Transformer whose core operation descends directly from learned soft alignment introduced here.
Q3.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - arXiv
Q3.falsification: This pass dies if a non-attention architecture, not the Transformer, powered the 2023 agent wave.

name: Deep Residual Learning (ResNet) (2015)
bottleneck: Before deep residual learning, training very deep networks was impractical because added layers degraded accuracy through optimization difficulty rather than overfitting.

Q2.evidence: Residual learning made networks of over 100 layers trainable, and the identity-shortcut pattern it unlocked is reused in every Transformer block to stack many layers.
Q2.source: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
Q2.falsification: if deep Transformer stacks had trained equally well with plain non-residual layers

name: Backpropagation (1986)
bottleneck: Before backpropagation, training multilayer neural networks was impractical because there was no efficient general method for assigning credit to hidden units.

Q2.evidence: Backpropagation made training arbitrary multilayer networks feasible, unlocking the entire deep-learning program of which the Transformer is one architecture.
Q2.source: Learning Representations by Back-Propagating Errors
Q2.falsification: if multilayer networks including Transformers had been trainable at scale by a comparably general non-gradient method

Q3.evidence: No ready substitute in 1986 or in 2017 could train deep networks with millions of parameters as generally as backpropagation, and the Transformer was trained with it via Adam.
Q3.falsification: if the original Transformer had been trained by a method not based on backpropagated gradients

name: Attention mechanism (Bahdanau)
bottleneck: Before the attention mechanism, neural sequence models were impractical on long inputs because a single fixed-length vector had to carry the entire source sequence.

Q1.evidence: Bahdanau et al. showed jointly learning to align and translate let the decoder use all source positions, sharply improving translation of long sentences that fixed-vector models degraded on.
Q1.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
Q1.falsification: if fixed-vector encoder-decoders had matched attention on long sentences

Q2.evidence: Attention generalized from an alignment add-on into self-attention, the sole sequence-mixing operation of the Transformer, unlocking the entire architecture family built on it.
Q2.source: Attention Is All You Need
Q2.falsification: if the Transformer had retained recurrence or convolution as its primary sequence mixer

name: Sequence-to-sequence learning (2014)
bottleneck: Before sequence-to-sequence learning, mapping an input sequence to an output sequence of different length with one end-to-end neural model was impractical because models required fixed-size inputs and task-specific alignment structure.

Q2.evidence: Sutskever et al. showed a single end-to-end LSTM encoder-decoder could translate whole sentences, framing translation and later tasks as generic sequence transduction that the Transformer directly inherited.
Q2.source: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
Q2.falsification: if the Transformer's encoder-decoder design were shown to derive independently of the seq2seq framing

name: Layer Normalization (2016)
bottleneck: Before Layer Normalization, normalizing recurrent and sequence networks was impractical because batch statistics depended on sequence length and batch composition.

Q2.evidence: Layer normalization made per-example normalization work for sequence models, and the Transformer embeds it in every sub-layer, enabling its deep stacks to train stably.
Q2.source: Layer Normalization
Q2.falsification: if the original Transformer had trained to its reported results using batch normalization or no normalization

name: Neural probabilistic language model (2003)
bottleneck: Before the neural probabilistic language model, statistical language modeling was crippled by the curse of dimensionality because n-gram models treated words as discrete symbols with no notion of similarity between them.

Q2.evidence: Bengio et al.'s model learned continuous distributed word representations jointly with the language model, opening the entire embedding-based research space that word2vec, and later the Transformer's learned token embeddings, grew from.
Q2.source: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if learned continuous word representations had not propagated beyond this paper into mainstream NLP practice.

name: Napier's logarithms (1614)
bottleneck: Before Napier's logarithms, computing with products and powers of probabilities was impractical because multiplication of many small numbers had no additive representation.

Q1.evidence: Logarithms converted multiplication into addition, making quantities like the log-probability of a sequence — the core of cross-entropy — computable and even conceivable as a sum at all.
Q1.falsification: if an additive representation of products in routine pre-1614 use is shown to have served the same role

Q2.evidence: Once log-probability exists as an additive quantity, entropy, cross-entropy, likelihood, and information measures all become definable from it.
Q2.source: Shannon, A Mathematical Theory of Communication (1948)
Q2.falsification: if Shannon's entropy is shown to be definable and used without logarithms

Q3.evidence: No pre-1614 substitute gave an additive measure of multiplicative quantities; prosthaphaeresis was a narrow trigonometric trick, not a general log function.
Q3.falsification: if a general pre-Napier log-equivalent is documented in practical use

name: Boltzmann's entropy formula (1877)
bottleneck: Before Boltzmann's entropy formula, entropy had no probabilistic definition because macroscopic entropy was not connected to the logarithm of the number of microstates.

Q2.evidence: Boltzmann's S = k log W made entropy a logarithm of a count/probability, the exact conceptual move Shannon generalized to -sum p log p and hence to cross-entropy.
Q2.source: Boltzmann, Über die Beziehung zwischen dem zweiten Hauptsatze der mechanischen Wärmetheorie und der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung (1877)
Q2.falsification: if Shannon's entropy is shown to owe nothing to the probabilistic entropy tradition Boltzmann founded

Q3.evidence: No substitute in 1877 expressed entropy probabilistically; Clausius's definition was macroscopic and gave no log-of-probability form for Shannon to generalize.
Q3.source: Boltzmann, Über die Beziehung zwischen dem zweiten Hauptsatze der mechanischen Wärmetheorie und der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung (1877)
Q3.falsification: if another pre-1877 source already defined entropy as a logarithm of probability

name: Fisher's maximum likelihood estimation (1922)
bottleneck: Before Fisher's maximum likelihood estimation, fitting a model distribution to data lacked a principled objective because there was no general criterion identifying the parameters that make the observed data most probable.

Q1.evidence: Maximizing log-likelihood is mathematically identical to minimizing cross-entropy between the empirical distribution and the model, so Fisher's 1922 framework supplied the exact optimization form cross-entropy loss later used.
Q1.source: Fisher, On the Mathematical Foundations of Theoretical Statistics (1922)
Q1.falsification: if maximizing log-likelihood were shown not to equal minimizing expected negative log-probability under the empirical distribution

Q2.evidence: Maximum likelihood gave a single general recipe for fitting any parametric distribution, unblocking estimation across statistics and later machine-learning classifiers.
Q2.source: Fisher, On the Mathematical Foundations of Theoretical Statistics (1922)
Q2.falsification: if pre-1922 practice already had an equally general parametric fitting recipe in routine use

Q3.evidence: No ready substitute in 1922 provided likelihood's generality, efficiency theory, and log-additive form; least squares covered only the Gaussian special case.
Q3.source: Fisher, On the Mathematical Foundations of Theoretical Statistics (1922)
Q3.falsification: if a contemporaneous general substitute with the same log form is shown to have been standard

name: Gibbs's statistical mechanics and Gibbs entropy (1902)
bottleneck: Before Gibbs's statistical mechanics, entropy for an arbitrary probability distribution over states was undefined because entropy existed only for specific physical systems, not as -sum p log p over any distribution.

Q1.evidence: Gibbs entropy, -k sum p_i log p_i, is formally identical to Shannon entropy and, with two distributions, to cross-entropy; it made a distributional log-loss quantity exist for the first time.
Q1.source: Gibbs, Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics (1902)
Q1.falsification: if Gibbs's 1902 text contains no entropy expressed as a sum of p log p over states

Q2.evidence: By defining entropy for any ensemble distribution, Gibbs unblocked the transfer of entropy from physics to any probabilistic system, including Shannon's message sources.
Q2.source: Gibbs, Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics (1902)
Q2.falsification: if Gibbs entropy is shown to apply only to one specific physical system

Q3.evidence: No pre-1902 substitute stated entropy as a functional of an arbitrary probability distribution; Boltzmann's form covered equiprobable microstates of a macrostate.
Q3.source: Gibbs, Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics (1902)
Q3.falsification: if an earlier author is shown to have published the general -sum p log p entropy

name: Hartley's logarithmic measure of information (1928)
bottleneck: Before Hartley's logarithmic measure of information, the amount of information in a message had no quantitative measure because no one had defined information as proportional to the logarithm of the number of possible sequences.

Q1.evidence: Hartley's 1928 H = n log s made information a measurable quantity for the first time, the direct problem Shannon generalized into entropy and cross-entropy.
Q1.falsification: if a quantitative logarithmic information measure is documented before 1928

Q2.evidence: Hartley's measure unblocked quantitative communication theory — channel capacity and coding — within which Shannon defined entropy and relative entropy/cross-entropy.
Q2.source: Shannon, A Mathematical Theory of Communication (1948)
Q2.falsification: if Shannon's 1948 theory is shown to make no use of Hartley's framework

Q3.evidence: Shannon explicitly built on Hartley as the predecessor measure; no rival 1928 information measure offered a substitute path.
Q3.source: Shannon, A Mathematical Theory of Communication (1948)
Q3.falsification: if Shannon is shown to have relied on a different predecessor measure instead of Hartley's

name: Huygens's expectation (1657)
bottleneck: Before Huygens's mathematical expectation, averaging a quantity over uncertain outcomes was impossible in principled form because probability had no expectation operator.

Q2.evidence: Expectation over a distribution is the outer operation of cross-entropy, H(p,q) = E_p[-log q]; Huygens's 1657 expected value made every later expected-loss quantity definable.
Q2.source: Huygens, De Ratiociniis in Ludo Aleae (1657)
Q2.falsification: if cross-entropy is shown to be definable without averaging -log q over the true distribution

Q3.evidence: No substitute for mathematical expectation existed in 1657; fair-price reasoning in games of chance was the only route to a probability-weighted average.
Q3.source: Huygens, De Ratiociniis in Ludo Aleae (1657)
Q3.falsification: if an equivalent expectation concept is documented in routine use before 1657
